answerer_note: ROUND 2 self-questioning turn: the finishing specialist answering itself in a fresh window, strictly and only from its own spec + KB1/KB2/KB3. Each answer carries [FACT]/[ESTIMATE]/[UNKNOWN] tags and names where in the spec it is grounded. Honesty binding respected: the three governing blockers (Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate, live blended CAC, forward India duty) plus the per-piece Ludhiana FINISHING job-work rate stay [UNKNOWN]; off-paper is mechanism, never accusation; cotton duty ~16.5%, never ~7%; the yarn floor dominates the finishing ceiling. Where the spec does not fully support an answer, specialist_supports=partial/no and the GAP is named honestly, never invented to look complete. Six of eleven land partial because R1 aimed precisely at joints the spec archetypes on pure fibres / substance-over-inline-label / a control step that is honestly conceded to be post-hoc.

answers.answer: Direction is grounded, the blend-fraction thresholds are a genuine GAP. My spec fixes A1 as a 'cotton-BLEND 12GG core' (specialist purpose; KB1/KB2/KB3 assumptions) yet writes the A1 recipe on the PURE-cotton archetype (A1_COTTON_RECIPE: gas-singe yarn + cellulase bio-polish garment, strength-capped). What I CAN state as [FACT] from the KBs: (a) gas-singe/gassing serves 'cotton and cotton-rich/viscose blends' and does NOT work on thermoplastic acrylic because a flame beads/melts it rather than cleanly singeing it (GASSING_SINGEING; MERCERISE_SINGE_YARN failure_modes); (b) cellulase bio-polish acts on 'cellulosics ONLY' and 'does nothing on acrylic or wool' (BIOPOLISH_CELLULASE; ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP). So on a 55/45 cotton/acrylic blend the DIRECTION is: singe only cleanly attacks the ~55% cellulosic fuzz and risks beading the ~45% thermoplastic fraction, and cellulase only de-fuzzes the cellulosic fraction, so the acrylic fraction's pilling is NOT controlled by either cotton route and must be won upstream via the low-pill/high-dpf acrylic grade + twist + gauge in the yarn PO (ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP route 4; A2_ACRYLIC_RECIPE logic imported). What I CANNOT give from my own spec: the numeric blend-fraction thresholds -- at what acrylic% singeing becomes disqualified by beading, and how much of the pure-cotton 'real grade' cellulase still buys at ~55% cellulosic. Those magnitudes are [UNKNOWN] pending PPS swatch testing on the actual A1 construction (PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH: per-construction uplift UNKNOWN). This is the yarn floor dominating the finishing ceiling on the blended article: a high-acrylic A1 with weak yarn-PO anti-pill grade is re-opened at the yarn spec, not rescued by piling cotton finishes onto a fraction they cannot touch.
answers.grounded_in: specialist purpose (A1 = cotton-BLEND); KB1 GASSING_SINGEING + BIOPOLISH_CELLULASE + ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP; KB2 A1_COTTON_RECIPE + MERCERISE_SINGE_YARN + ANTIPILL_ROUTES route 4; KB3 PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH (per-construction uplift UNKNOWN)
answers.gap_note: The four anti-pill routes and the A1 recipe are written on PURE-fibre archetypes, but A1 SHIPS as a cotton-blend. The fibre-chemistry DIRECTIONS transfer cleanly (singe fails on the thermoplastic fraction, cellulase touches only the cellulosic fraction, acrylic pilling is a yarn-PO lever), but no numeric blend-fraction threshold is specified for when singe is disqualified or how much cellulase buys at a given cellulosic share. A per-article blend caveat (state the A1 blend ratio explicitly in the recipe and route the acrylic-fraction pilling to the yarn PO, magnitudes UNKNOWN pending PPS) is a real, uninvented content gap -- a 'propose' fix, not something to fabricate a threshold for.

answers.answer: My spec closes the SKIPPED-step seam but not the STACKED-route attribution seam -- a genuine GAP. What is grounded: the two-PO recipe requires BOTH POs to carry the SAME post-wash ICI + shrinkage gate 'or a step skipped at one vendor quietly passes the test at the other' (TWO_PO_RECIPE / TWO_PO_STRUCTURE), which catches a route entirely omitted at the wrong vendor. My ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP CON explicitly concedes 'a rigid four-route map can hide that several routes stack on one cotton garment' (A1 uses gas-singe AND cellulase). What is NOT grounded: when a stacked A1 lot fails ICI post-wash with both routes nominally applied, my spec has NO per-route diagnostic to separate singe-skipped-at-the-spinner from enzyme-underdosed-at-the-finisher. The nearest instrument I own is partial: the mandatory A1 retained bursting/tensile-strength check (RETAINED_STRENGTH_CAP; ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 4) is bio-polish-specific, so a strength READING in-spec alongside a pilling FAIL points at under-processed cellulase rather than singe, and a yarn-lot hairiness/singe read lives on the yarn PO -- but I do not compose these into an attribution rule. So the honest answer is: I must NOT reflexively 'blame the spinner.' Where the diagnostic evidence is silent, the correct move is to code the mixed fail back on BOTH POs and require a per-route swatch re-test (singed-yarn-only vs bio-polished-garment) to isolate it, not to charge the cheaper-to-blame vendor. Attribution by reflex would mis-charge a finisher fault to the yarn PO or vice-versa.
answers.grounded_in: KB3 TWO_PO_RECIPE + ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP CON (stacked routes) + ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 4 / RETAINED_STRENGTH_CAP; KB2 TWO_PO_STRUCTURE; conflicts_and_dominance 'yarn-PO floor versus finishing ceiling'
answers.gap_note: The shared post-wash gate resolves 'a skipped step passes at the wrong vendor' but NOT the attribution of a mixed/stacked pilling fail where both routes were nominally applied. The spec offers only an indirect signal (the A1 strength check flags cellulase over/under-processing) and otherwise risks defaulting to 'the yarn floor dominates' as a blame-direction rather than a fault-isolation procedure. A per-route diagnostic step (isolate with a singed-yarn-only and a bio-polished-garment swatch re-test; code back on both POs until isolated) is a real missing procedure, not an invented number -- 'propose'.

answers.answer: Reading a cardinal A1>A2>A3 efficacy ranking off 'half a grade' to prioritise finishing spend is an OVER-CLAIM, and my node substantively resists it but does not hard-stop it. What is grounded and correct: FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA holds the uplift MAGNITUDES LOW and the DIRECTIONS HIGH, states A1 HIGH / A2 FRACTIONAL / A3 CRAFT-DEPENDENT as a directional read, and its own failure_modes explicitly name 'treating the efficacy magnitudes as measured rather than directional' and 'using a high A1 efficacy to justify finishing a cheap yarn elsewhere.' PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH reinforces that per-construction ICI uplift is [UNKNOWN] until PPS swatch testing, and escalation_triggers[4] says any uplift asserted 'as a magnitude rather than a direction' must DEFER, keeping 'half a grade' a convenient round number, not a measurement. So the in-spec use is ORDINAL/DIRECTIONAL only (which route earns its place per article), never a decision-grade cardinal number fed into a spend model. Where the node is weaker than it should be: (a) it self-describes as one that 'recomputes its derived scores from its base metrics,' which invites a reader to treat the recomputed score as cardinal; (b) it does NOT force its OUTPUT to be LABELED ordinal/directional -- the label lives in the definition prose and the failure_modes, not as a hard output contract; and (c) human_review_required=false removes the human backstop on exactly this node. So: in-spec = ordinal read for route selection; out-of-spec = any cardinal A1-vs-A2-vs-A3 number fed to T4 to size finishing spend. The magnitudes stay [UNKNOWN] until PPS.
answers.grounded_in: KB3 FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA (directions HIGH/magnitudes LOW, recompute-derived-scores, human_review_required=false, failure_modes) + PILLING_GATE_POSTWASH (uplift UNKNOWN); escalation_triggers[4] (uplift-as-magnitude -> defer); router N1/N6
answers.gap_note: The efficacy node self-guards in substance (directions HIGH / magnitudes LOW; failure_modes name the cardinal-read abuse and the finish-a-cheap-yarn abuse) but does NOT force its output label to ORDINAL/directional, and human_review_required=false removes the backstop on the one node most likely to be mis-read as a decision-grade number. The over-claim is latent in the node contract, not in the answer. Minimal fix (apply-able): set human_review_required=true on FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA and add an explicit 'output is ORDINAL/directional, not a cardinal decision-grade score; magnitudes UNKNOWN pending PPS' contract line.

answers.answer: The band carries its honesty guard in SUBSTANCE but not as one inline method+basis+confidence string -- a real labelling gap. What is grounded: COST_OF_QUALITY_TRADE gives per-article bands ~$0.30-0.90 (A1) / ~$0.25-0.70 (A2) / ~$0.60-1.80 (A3), tagged '[ESTIMATE: triangulated, ordering sound]' with 'the ordering HIGH, the absolute numbers LOW,' and JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER names the per-piece Ludhiana finishing job-work rate as [UNKNOWN] blocking the T4 bottom-up model, stating the absolute numbers 'must NOT be fed as points into T4 without a live quote.' So the [ESTIMATE] is the triangulated band + the A3>A1>A2 ORDERING; the [UNKNOWN] is the per-piece finishing job-work rate at a named finisher (sister to T1's linking rate and T2's dye-lot MOQ). What stops a T4 reader from lifting the band as decision points is exactly the JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER 'do-not-feed-as-points' instruction plus escalation_triggers[0] (defer on the per-piece rate). On WHY the ordering is [ESTIMATE]-grade even with the absolute rate [UNKNOWN]: it rests on the fibre-route step content, not on the missing rate -- A3 is the buy-the-craft milling+boarding job (most skilled/irreversible wet steps), A1 adds a garment cellulase bio-polish bath (a real extra wet step), and A2 buys only a light chemical/silicone top-up + hand (fewest added steps), so A3>A1>A2 follows from route composition (FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA; the three per-article recipes). That basis is present in the KBs but is NOT spelled out INLINE at the cost band as a method string, so a careless reader sees an ordering without its derivation. Honest status: substance-correct, inline-label incomplete.
answers.grounded_in: KB3 COST_OF_QUALITY_TRADE (bands + ordering-HIGH/absolutes-LOW) + JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER (per-piece rate UNKNOWN, do-not-feed-as-points) + FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA (route composition); boundaries[0]; escalation_triggers[0]; router N1/N2
answers.gap_note: The cost band is genuinely tagged [ESTIMATE] with ordering-HIGH/absolutes-LOW and a do-not-feed-as-points blocker, so the guard exists -- but it is not condensed into one inline method+basis+confidence derivation at the point of the number, and the ordering's evidentiary basis (A3>A1>A2 from wet-step count/skill/irreversibility, independent of the UNKNOWN rate) is implied across nodes rather than stated at the band. Minimal fix (apply-able): add an inline 'method=triangulated by route step-content; basis=A3 milling+boarding > A1 +cellulase bath > A2 chemical top-up; confidence: ordering HIGH, absolutes LOW; per-piece rate UNKNOWN -- not a T4 point' string.

answers.answer: My composition check flags the drift and states the duty EXPOSURE, then routes the landed/IOR adjudication out of my lane -- and it already carries the corrected trio, never ~7%. Grounded verbatim in FASTNESS_DELTAE_COMPOSITION (check 5 of the eight-check gate): a fibre-composition test vs the care label is 'also the duty exposure -- blend drift (e.g. 70/30 +/-3% by mass) is both a quiet cost-down and a duty-misdeclaration risk for us as importer of record (wool 6110.11 ~16% vs cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5%, while acrylic/MMF 6110.30.30 ~32% is the outlier, and crossing 50% MMF by chief weight flips a 'cotton' sweater to that 32% line).' So when I catch a 70/30-drifted-to-60/40 blend: (1) I state the duty numbers only as the CORRECTED [FACT] trio -- cotton ~16.5% (NEVER ~7%), wool ~16%, acrylic/MMF ~32%, with the chief-weight cliff at 50% MMF; (2) I do NOT adjudicate the landed/IOR/duty CONSEQUENCE -- that is unit_economics' lane per the dominance rule (landed cost/duty/IOR = unit_economics); (3) my action is FLAG-AND-ROUTE: code the composition fail back to the named supplier as a garment-gate defect (it is a real defect a tiny brand cannot eat) AND surface the drift as an IOR blend-drift/duty-misdeclaration flag handed to unit_economics, who owns the number and the Importer-of-Record liability. The dye node stays outsourced (T1). So the check legitimately TOUCHES duty exposure without RECITING a rate I own beyond the corrected anchor and without crossing into the landed calc.
answers.grounded_in: KB3 FASTNESS_DELTAE_COMPOSITION (composition-vs-label check, corrected duty trio ~16.5/~16/~32, chief-weight 50% MMF cliff, IOR blend-drift framing, dye node outsourced); router dominance 'landed cost/duty = unit_economics'; router N5 (~16.5% never ~7%) / N2-N3 (IOR blend-drift)
answers.gap_note: None material. The composition check is correctly scoped as flag-and-route: it names the duty EXPOSURE with the corrected [FACT] trio (~16.5% cotton, never the discredited ~7%) and the chief-weight cliff, but defers the landed/IOR/duty CONSEQUENCE to unit_economics, keeping the finishing gate on the defect side and the P&L on the owner's side.

answers.answer: I outsource the milling machine and gate it POST-HOC, and my spec honestly concedes that the real control is the finisher's craft, not my gate -- so the control claim is bounded, not over-reached. Grounded: OUTSOURCE_BOUNDARY / OUTSOURCE_WET_POSTURE outsources 100% of wet/skilled/regulated steps including milling; A3_WOOL_RECIPE routes A3 'to a SPECIALIST wool finisher; own spec + gate'; MILLING_GATE states milling is wool-only, irreversible, 'the single most destructive finishing failure,' gated on DIMENSIONS + a FELT/AREA-SHRINK LIMIT + HAND 'never to the clock,' with time the short dial -- AND it explicitly says 'the real A3 risk is in-cluster wool-finishing skill and capacity ... not the recipe, because felt-control is the whole game,' and JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER carries wool-milling felt-control reliability as an [UNKNOWN]. So how I actually control an outsourced irreversible run: NOT in real time -- I concede I cannot stand on the floor. My control is (a) up-front: specify the felt/area-shrink limit + dimensions + hand as the stop condition in the finishing PO, and select a proven SPECIALIST wool finisher whose felt-control craft is the qualification; (b) sampled: dial the setpoint in on PPS/first-piece before bulk; (c) post-hoc: the A3-mandatory milling felt/area-shrink-limit check in the eight-check gate (ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 6) REJECTS a felted lot after the fact. The honest limit: the gate is post-hoc, so an over-milled A3 lot is already dead wool when it fails -- unsalvageable premium inventory (working-capital trap). 'Route to a specialist wool finisher' is therefore an admission that felt-control is bought craft I cannot gate in real time, not owned control; the gate protects the NEXT lot and the contractual code-back, and vendor selection + PPS dial-in are the only pre-loss levers I hold.
answers.grounded_in: KB2 MILLING_GATE (irreversible, gated on felt/area-shrink not clock, real risk = in-cluster skill/capacity) + A3_WOOL_RECIPE (outsource to specialist wool finisher) + OUTSOURCE_BOUNDARY; KB3 ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 6 (A3 milling felt-limit mandatory) + JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER (felt-control reliability UNKNOWN); conflicts_and_dominance 'milling versus irreversible felting'; escalation_triggers[1]
answers.gap_note: The spec is honest that outsourcing removes real-time control of the one irreversible garment-destroying step and that the gate is post-hoc (it rejects a felted lot AFTER the wool is dead), and it names in-cluster felt-control skill/capacity as the [UNKNOWN] real risk. The residual gap is not a contradiction but an unclosable exposure: pre-loss protection reduces to vendor selection + PPS/first-piece dial-in, and there is no arms-length in-run control mechanism. This is a genuine limitation to state plainly (and to price into A3 working-capital risk), not something to paper over with a false 'we gate it' claim.

answers.answer: It is currently an UNCONFIRMED working target treated as a pass/fail line, and my spec flags the risk but does not carry the [UNKNOWN]-pending-buyer tag ON the gate threshold -- a real labelling gap. Grounded: SHRINKAGE_GATE accepts 'within +/-3-5% (confirm per buyer) after the same [home] wash,' ties it to factory wet-relax + compact, and explicitly 'flags the tumble-dry US household tighter-limit risk'; escalation_triggers[5] says the +/-3-5% target 'may be tightened by a tumble-dry US customer and must be confirmed per buyer before it gates a lot'; RELAX_SHRINK_CONTROL/RELAX_COMPACT sets the +/-3-5% as a 'working target.' The Turlock/California consumer is a warm-climate tumble-dry household (specialist purpose; SCOPE_GLOSSARY: warm California market). So the honest status: the +/-3-5% is an [ESTIMATE: working target] and its buyer-confirmed value is [UNKNOWN] until confirmed; my spec says 'confirm per buyer BEFORE it gates a lot,' which means it should NOT yet be gating as a hard confirmed line. Why it is nonetheless in the acceptance gate: as a provisional/placeholder tolerance to be tightened, NOT as a signed-off threshold -- but the gate node presents +/-3-5% as the accept band without carrying an explicit [UNKNOWN]-pending-buyer STATUS TAG on the number, so a careless reader could pass a lot at +/-4% that a tumble-dry US customer would reject. The correct posture: hold the threshold [UNKNOWN]-pending-buyer, gate provisionally at the tighter end for a tumble-dry household until confirmed, and mirror the customer's EXACT wash+dry cycle (the same-wash rule in SHRINKAGE_GATE).
answers.grounded_in: KB3 SHRINKAGE_GATE (+/-3-5% confirm-per-buyer, tumble-dry tighter-limit risk, same-wash rule) + RELAX_SHRINK_CONTROL working target; escalation_triggers[5]; specialist purpose (warm-climate Turlock/California, tumble-dry)
answers.gap_note: The +/-3-5% dimensional tolerance is admittedly a working target that 'may be tightened' and 'must be confirmed per buyer before it gates a lot,' yet it sits in the acceptance gate as the accept band without carrying an explicit [UNKNOWN]-pending-buyer status tag on the threshold. For the Turlock tumble-dry household this risks a lot passing green while failing the real customer. Minimal fix (apply-able): tag the shrinkage threshold [UNKNOWN]-pending-buyer, gate provisionally at the tighter end for a tumble-dry cycle, and require the buyer-confirmed value + the exact wash+dry cycle before it becomes a hard pass/fail line.

answers.answer: Whose PO owns it: the yarn PO. What my gate does: DETECT and ROUTE, never fix -- and calling the fix a 'balanced-ply yarn decision' routes it correctly to yarn_sourcing without me pretending a finishing rescue exists. Grounded verbatim: SPIRALITY_SISTER_FAULT reads spirality (twisted side-seam) as 'the post-wash exposure of an unbalanced singles-twist yarn-PO dial (T2 dial 2, balanced ply), NOT a finishing defect of its own ... worst on singles ... The gate reads it (visual + skew after wash, within tolerance) but cannot FIX it; the fix is upstream balanced ply in the yarn PO.' Its own CON concedes 'reading-not-fixing spirality offers no garment-side remedy once a bad-twist lot is already knit' -- a skewed lot 'can only be coded back, not finished out, so the cost is already sunk.' So when a finished lot fails spirality post-wash: (1) the defect is real and read at ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 3 (spirality/twisted side-seam after wash); (2) I do NOT claim a finishing correction -- pressing/steaming a wale-skewed singles lot does not remove torque-driven spirality; (3) I code it back to the named supplier and route the FIX to the yarn PO balanced-ply dial (yarn_sourcing owns fibre/yarn PO per the dominance rule). This is the clearest case of the gate exposing a yarn-floor failure the finishing line cannot rescue, reinforcing the second-line principle -- so there is no silent acceptance of a finishing rescue I cannot deliver.
answers.grounded_in: KB3 SPIRALITY_SISTER_FAULT (read-not-fix, unbalanced singles-twist yarn-PO dial, code-back, cost already sunk) + ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 3; glossary 'spirality (balanced-ply sister fault)'; conflicts_and_dominance yarn-floor-dominates; router dominance 'fibre/yarn PO = yarn_sourcing'
answers.gap_note: None material on attribution/routing: spirality is correctly framed as detect-at-gate / fix-upstream-at-the-yarn-PO-balanced-ply-dial, with no false finishing rescue implied. The only honest residual (already stated in the node's CON) is that there is no garment-side remedy once a bad-twist lot is knit -- the cost is sunk and the value is the code-back plus the yarn-PO correction for the next lot, not a save of the failed lot.

answers.answer: Where it is caught: at the post-wash hand/softener-durability check, after the SAME home wash. The test condition that defeats it: grade hand AFTER >=1 home wash, never in the freshly-softened showroom state. The authority question is where my spec is thinner. Grounded: HOME_WASH_PROMISE / SOFTENER_HAND states silicone gives 'the expensive 3-second hand' but 'softener can MASK a harsh yarn, so a heavily-softened sample feels great in the showroom and harsh after one wash,' so the gate 'tests hand and dimensions AFTER the same home wash ... never in the freshly-softened showroom state'; ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 5 is 'Hand/softener durability -- hand after wash, not in the showroom'; boundaries[5] requires every claim to 'survive the named post-wash test ... never present a showroom-fresh hand or pilling read as the acceptance result'; conflicts_and_dominance holds 'the post-wash gate dominates the showroom sample' and 'a wash-durable softener tested after a wash dominates ... masking is rejected.' So a masked sample is caught the moment the wash-durability check runs post-wash and the hand goes harsh. On the authority to reject a lot that MATCHES a buyer-approved freshly-softened reference: my conflict-dominance rule asserts post-wash dominates the showroom sample, which is my STANDING position -- but my spec does not explicitly resolve the contractual case where the APPROVED reference sample is itself the masked, freshly-softened one. The honest reading: my rule gives me the basis to reject on the post-wash gate, but the fix is procedural and not fully written -- the buyer-approved reference must ITSELF be a post-wash-graded sample, or the masked approval stands and my gate is asserting authority it has not contractually secured. So: caught technically yes; authority asserted but not fully operationalised against a masked approved reference.
answers.grounded_in: KB3 HOME_WASH_PROMISE + ACCEPTANCE_GATE_EIGHT_CHECKS check 5; KB1/KB2 SOFTENING_HAND/SOFTENER_HAND (masking trap); boundaries[5]; conflicts_and_dominance 'showroom-fresh versus post-wash' + 'softener-delivered hand versus masking'
answers.gap_note: The masking trap is caught technically (hand/softener-durability graded post-wash, showroom-fresh read forbidden) and post-wash dominance is my standing rule, but the spec does not close the contractual loop where the buyer-APPROVED reference sample is itself the freshly-softened masked one -- a lot matching that reference could pass sign-off while failing my post-wash gate, and my authority to reject it is asserted, not operationalised. Minimal fix (apply-able): require the approved reference/PPS sample to be POST-WASH-graded (approve on the washed hand, not the showroom hand), so the gate and the sign-off reference share the same post-wash condition and the authority is contractual, not merely asserted.

answers.answer: The mechanism, stated structurally with no firm/person, no tax-evasion allegation, and no magnitude: in a fragmented micro-unit cluster, cash job-work finishing can be cheaper because the job-work mesh lets a specialised wet step be rented per-garment rather than carried as owned fixed-cost kit (OUTSOURCE_BOUNDARY: 'outsourcing converts a fixed-cost machine into a per-garment job-work charge'), and the general cluster conditions -- thin margins, high competition, cash-heavy local trade, informal/contract labour, and discretionary interaction with inspectors where enforcement is patchy -- create structural INCENTIVES for informal cash transactions (SCOPE_GLOSSARY 9 off-paper mechanism; boundaries[6] 'cash job-work, informal labour, discretionary inspection where enforcement is patchy'). That is as far as I go: it is a structural incentive and a hypothesis to probe, MEDIUM confidence such mechanisms exist in clusters generally, LOW/[UNKNOWN] on magnitude in Ludhiana specifically, and I allege NO named party does any of it. I explicitly do NOT put a number on any off-paper 'discount' -- inventing one would both fabricate and accuse, and the per-piece Ludhiana finishing job-work rate stays [UNKNOWN] as a named blocker (JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER). Where the substantive off-paper read actually lives: it is the Ludhiana T1 sourcing specialist's lane, not mine (router dominance 'off-paper economy = ludhiana_sourcing_strategist'; boundaries[4]/[6] route the regulated/cluster-economy boundary to T1). So: mechanism named at the level my scope permits, magnitude [UNKNOWN], substantive analysis deferred to Ludhiana -- and I stop there.
answers.grounded_in: boundaries[6] (off-paper as mechanism) + boundaries[4] (route regulated boundary to T1); KB2 OUTSOURCE_BOUNDARY (per-garment job-work charge); JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER (rate UNKNOWN); SCOPE_GLOSSARY 9; router N3 + dominance 'off-paper = ludhiana_sourcing'
answers.gap_note: None material -- and this is a defer-by-design, not a hole. The off-paper mechanism is describable structurally within my boundaries (per-garment job-work vs owned kit; general cluster cash/informal-labour/patchy-enforcement incentives), all magnitudes [UNKNOWN], no named-party accusation. The substantive off-paper economy read is the Ludhiana T1 specialist's lane; I name the mechanism at my scope and route the depth to T1 rather than over-answering or inventing a discount magnitude.

answers.answer: Merged A2 finishing go/no-go: finishing spend earns a LIMITED, minimal place on A2, and my verdict must DEFER viability, not imply a GO. Grounded finishing verdict: on A2 fine-acrylic the ICI grade is won or lost at the YARN PO, not the finishing line -- acrylic is thermoplastic (can't be cleanly singed) and non-cellulosic (cellulase does nothing), so finishing buys only a chemical/silicone FRACTION of a grade plus the hand + home-wash dimensional experience (A2_ACRYLIC_RECIPE; ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP; HOME_WASH_PROMISE; FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA: A2 FRACTIONAL). The one decisive dial on A2 is the softener-stiffness ceiling (chemical anti-pill can stiffen the hand), and if forced onto cheap acrylic the fix is to RE-OPEN THE YARN SPEC, not pile on anti-pill (conflicts_and_dominance; RECIPE_GO_NOGO). So finishing spend on A2 is 'yes, but minimal and only for hand + measurements + the fractional top-up' -- NOT a claim that finishing rescues A2 pilling. On viability: this is where I must NOT let 'finishing is a small minority cost slice' (COST_OF_QUALITY_TRADE) imply the venture makes money. Viability is NOT my lane -- it is decided on contribution-margin-after-CAC by unit_economics + the DECISION_MEMO (router dominance), which carry the GATED-conditional-GO posture: dead as first drawn (value-led, A2-acrylic-hero, cold-paid-social), and A2 is the brand-ending pilling case gated on G4 (ICI >=3-4 post-wash on our actual A2 construction, [UNKNOWN]-UNTESTED) with the cost foundation gated on G2 (knit+LINK per-piece rate, [UNKNOWN]) and my own per-piece finishing job-work rate [UNKNOWN] (JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER). The [UNKNOWN] blocker I carry is the per-piece Ludhiana finishing job-work rate; the pilling blocker is G4-on-A2 (won at the yarn PO, finishing buys only a fraction). So: finishing on A2 = spec it LIGHT, win the grade upstream, gate G4 hard; viability = deferred to unit_economics/DECISION_MEMO under the GATED-conditional-GO posture, inventory cash FORBIDDEN until G1-G4 pass -- no naive GO leaks from 'finishing is cheap.'
answers.grounded_in: KB1/KB2 A2_ACRYLIC_RECIPE + ANTIPILL_ROUTE_MAP + HOME_WASH_PROMISE + FINISHING_EFFICACY_FORMULA (A2 fractional) + COST_OF_QUALITY_TRADE + JOBWORK_RATE_BLOCKER + RECIPE_GO_NOGO; capability 'merge into labeled-estimate go/no-go'; router N7 + dominance 'viability = unit_economics + DECISION_MEMO' + the four hard gates G2/G4
